Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n```lean\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\n  match g with\n  | some p => p.poly\n  | none   => 0\n```\n\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\n\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The failure mode this guards against is subtle: a development\\\\\\\\nthat compiles, shows zero `Admitted`, and still certifies the wrong theorem\\\\\\\\nbecause a quantifier moved, a constant halved, or a hypothesis quietly\\\\\\\\nassumed the hard part.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Ground rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Read-only.** Do not edit proof files, TeX, or mapping files during the\\\\\\\\n  audit. An audit that fixes as it goes destroys its own evidence and tempts\\\\\\\\n  you to patch a symptom (the constant) before the cause (a hypothesis\\\\\\\\n  mismatch) is characterized. If the prompt asks to *fix* faithfulness, run\\\\\\\\n  the full audit on the item first, present the report, then edit only what\\\\\\\\n  the report flags.\\\\\\\\n- **Project docs win.** Read the project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / README\\\\\\\\n  first. If they prescribe a mapping file, an accepted-axiom whitelist, a\\\\\\\\n  verdict vocabulary, or a route-fidelity requirement, those override the\\\\\\\\n  defaults below.\\\\\\\\n- **Compilation is not faithfulness.** Never report \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"faithful\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" from a green\\\\\\\\n  build; every verdict needs statement-level evidence you quote in the report.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Procedure\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Locate the audit index\\\\\\\\nLook for a mapping file (e.g. `ownership.md`) that maps formal source files\\\\\\\\nto TeX sections; if present it defines the item list and the anchors — use it\\\\\\\\nas-is. Otherwise build the index yourself: enumerate theorem/lemma/definition\\\\\\\\nnames in the formal sources, grep the TeX for `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\begin{theorem}`, `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\label`,\\\\\\\\nequation tags, and pair them by name, comment, or content. List anything you\\\\\\\\ncannot pair under \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Unmapped\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" — unmapped items are findings, not noise.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. Run five checks per item\\\\\\\\n1. **Statement match.** Put the TeX statement and the formal statement side\\\\\\\\n   by side. Compare quantifier order and scope, constants and exponents,\\\\\\\\n   inequality direction and strictness, side conditions (`n >= 1`, `eps > 0`,\\\\\\\\n   normalization), and implicit conventions (log base, probability space,\\\\\\\\n   adversary model). These are exactly the places a formalization drifts\\\\\\\\n   while staying well-typed and provable, so check them term by term.\\\\\\\\n2. **Proof-route match, where the project demands it.** If the project claims\\\\\\\\n   to formalize *the paper's proof* (check the docs and paper text for that\\\\\\\\n   claim), confirm the formal proof follows the paper's decomposition — same\\\\\\\\n   key lemmas, same argument — not an alternative shortcut. A shortcut can\\\\\\\\n   prove a superficially identical statement whose meaning has shifted (e.g.\\\\\\\\n   a weaker adversary model makes the bound trivial), and it forfeits the\\\\\\\\n   claim that the paper's argument is machine-checked. If the docs make no\\\\\\\\n   route claim, note route divergence as an observation, not a failure.\\\\\\\\n3. **No silent strengthening or weakening.** Diff hypotheses and conclusion\\\\\\\\n   against the TeX. A *paper-level\\\\\\\\n   abstraction* works at the same level the paper does (classical reals,\\\\\\\\n   finite dimensions when the paper is finite-dimensional, standard-library\\\\\\\\n   classical axioms the project whitelists) and may stand. A *cheating\\\\\\\\n   assumption* assumes something the paper proves, or something stronger than\\\\\\\\n   the paper assumes, and must be discharged before the result can be\\\\\\\\n   claimed. The distinction is what the whole audit turns on — when unsure,\\\\\\\\n   ask what the paper's referee would say if shown the assumption.\\\\\\\\n5. **Hypothesis provenance.** Before compiling anything for the closure\\\\\\\\n   check, look for a running build (`pgrep -fl 'coqc|dune|lake|make'`) and\\\\\\\\n   reuse fresh compiled artifacts; keep at most 2 live prover processes.\\\\\\\\n   Compute the assumption closure of each top-level theorem — `Print\\\\\\\\n   Assumptions <thm>.` in Coq/Rocq, `#print axioms <thm>` in Lean — and grep\\\\\\\\n   the dependency files for\\\\\\\\n   `Admitted|admit|Axiom|Parameter|Hypothesis|sorry`. Nuance:\\\\\\\\n   `Hypothesis`/`Variable` inside a Section are discharged into the\\\\\\\\n   statement (premises, not taint), and `Parameter`/`Axiom` inside a\\\\\\\\n   `Module Type` is an interface declaration — classify these separately;\\\\\\\\n   only declarations that appear in the Print Assumptions closure are\\\\\\\\n   candidate taint. Scale to the item count\\\\\\\\nFor large indices, spawn parallel subagents if available (one per TeX section\\\\\\\\nor source file) and merge their tables; otherwise iterate sequentially. In\\\\\\\\neither case run the provenance commands in a shell yourself, so verdicts rest\\\\\\\\non tool output rather than on reading the sources.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Verdicts\\\\\\\\n- **faithful** — statement matches (and route, where required); assumption\\\\\\\\n  closure is empty or whitelisted by project docs.\\\\\\\\n- **divergent** — statement differs materially from the TeX, or the route\\\\\\\\n  diverges where the project demands route fidelity.\\\\\\\\n- **cheat** — depends on an undischarged cheating assumption.\\\\\\\\n- **unproven** — the item or something in its closure is `Admitted`/`sorry`.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAn item receives the worst verdict among its findings.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Output format\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n## Faithfulness audit — <formal target> vs <TeX source>\\\\\\\\nIndex: <mapping file used, or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"built ad hoc\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\">   Scope: <files / sections>\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Formal name (file:line) | Source anchor | Verdict | Evidence | Required action |\\\\\\\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\\\\\\\n| fail_bound (security.v:88) | Thm 4.2, Eq. The `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}` tag is the link; the body text is standard mathematics. If you can't say it in math, rewrite it.\\\\\\\\n4. **No filler prose.** Only precise definitions, theorem statements, and proof sketches. No \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"this is important because...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the self-improvement step governs the induction...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\n5. **Cite non-trivial things.** Basic definitions don't need citations. Important results and non-obvious definitions should cite the source paper.\\\\\\\\n6. **Don't invent terminology or notation.** Don't create ad-hoc notation when standard notation exists. Don't name things that the literature doesn't name.\\\\\\\\n7. **Match Lean's theorem/lemma/def exactly.** If Lean says `theorem X`, use `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\begin{theorem}`. If Lean says `lemma X`, use `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\begin{lemma}`. `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\begin{proposition}` is allowed in blueprint prose when it improves mathematical readability, but still map it to an actual Lean `theorem`/`lemma` declaration via `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}`. Label prefix: `thm:` for theorem, `lem:` for lemma, `def:` for definition, `prop:` for proposition.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Remark On Mathematical Prose\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBlueprint entries should read as mathematical exposition, not as progress\\\\\\\\nreports. The mathematical argument should determine the order of the prose:\\\\\\\\nintroduce the notation, state the assertion, give the proof or calculation, and\\\\\\\\nthen record Lean references through the usual blueprint tags. Lean declarations,\\\\\\\\nfile paths, and proof-status information should not become the visible structure\\\\\\\\nof the paragraph. When referring to a source article, cite it bibliographically\\\\\\\\nrather than relying on an uncited reference to the article.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse displayed formulae when the formula benefits from visual separation, and\\\\\\\\nkeep short scalar definitions or elementary inequalities inline when the\\\\\\\\nsentence reads better that way. As in ordinary mathematical writing, displayed\\\\\\\\nformulae should be punctuated as part of the sentences in which they occur.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Proof Sketches Must Match Lean\\\\\\\\nThis is the most important rule. Every proof in the blueprint must faithfully describe what the Lean proof does:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Reference the actual lemmas used.** If the Lean proof calls `LDT.selfImprovement`, the blueprint proof should say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"By Lemma X.Y (self-improvement)...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and list it in `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\uses`.\\\\\\\\n- **Do not use `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\cref` or `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\Cref`.** The blueprint does not load `cleveref`.\\\\\\\\n  Spell out the kind of object and use ordinary references, for example\\\\\\\\n  `Lemma~\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ref{lem:self-improvement}` or `Theorem~\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ref{thm:main-formal}`.\\\\\\\\n- **Describe the actual proof structure.** If Lean does induction on a parameter, say so. If Lean uses a specific decomposition, name it.\\\\\\\\n- **Don't hand-wave where Lean is specific.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Standard argument\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is not acceptable if Lean uses three specific lemmas. Name them.\\\\\\\\n- **Don't be more specific than Lean.** If Lean uses `simp` to close a goal, a one-line sketch is fine.\\\\\\\\n- **`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\uses` in proofs must be accurate.** Only list what the proof actually uses, not what the statement mentions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Source-Labelled Statements And Conditional Helpers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf a blueprint theorem, lemma, or proposition carries a source label from the\\\\\\\\npaper, the linked Lean declaration must state the same theorem, up to faithful\\\\\\\\nformal encoding of the paper's domain.  Do not use `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}` and `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`\\\\\\\\non the source-labelled statement to point to a conditional helper whose\\\\\\\\nadditional assumptions supply an unproved part of the paper proof.\\\\\\\\nChanging the Lean statement away from `references/ldt-paper/` is strongly\\\\\\\\ndiscouraged unless faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical\\\\\\\\nnecessity requires it; the blueprint should make any such necessity explicit.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBoundary hypotheses such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,\\\\\\\\npositivity of parameters, and denominator nonvanishing may be faithful when\\\\\\\\nthey express the mathematical domain that the paper leaves implicit.  By\\\\\\\\ncontrast, bridge inputs, residual data, repair hypotheses, producer\\\\\\\\nassumptions, proof-obligation inputs, or package assumptions are proof debt.\\\\\\\\nThey must not be added to a source-labelled theorem statement.  If such data is\\\\\\\\nstill unproved, the source-labelled Lean theorem should keep the source-shaped\\\\\\\\nstatement and carry a tracked `sorry`, or the missing assertion should appear\\\\\\\\nas the lowest named internal obligation with a tracked `sorry`.  A separately\\\\\\\\nnamed conditional helper should not be introduced as a repair pattern.  If one\\\\\\\\nalready contains substantial proof content, it may remain temporarily only as\\\\\\\\nquarantine: it needs a paper source, a tracking issue, and a discharge or\\\\\\\\ndeletion plan.  The blueprint should leave the paper theorem unmarked as\\\\\\\\nproof-complete until the source-faithful Lean statement has a source-faithful\\\\\\\\nproof.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf a Lean theorem proves only a restricted version of a source theorem, the\\\\\\\\nblueprint entry carrying `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` must state that restriction in the theorem\\\\\\\\nstatement itself.  It must not be cited as the unrestricted source theorem.\\\\\\\\nWhen the only Lean declaration available for a source label has extra\\\\\\\\nnon-paper assumptions, remove the `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` claim from the source-labelled\\\\\\\\nentry or move the restricted statement to a separate Lean-only entry.  The\\\\\\\\nunrestricted paper theorem remains unformalized until a Lean statement with\\\\\\\\nthe source's hypothesis set exists.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Notation Consistency\\\\\\\\nNotation must be **internally consistent** across the entire blueprint and **close to what the Lean code expresses**:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Indices**: 0-indexed where matching `Fin n` in Lean\\\\\\\\n- **Finite fields / alphabets**: use standard notation for the alphabet $\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\Sigma$ and finite fields $\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\mathbb{F}_q$\\\\\\\\n- **Measurements**: use standard quantum measurement notation (projective measurements, POVMs)\\\\\\\\n- **Strategies**: quantum strategies for nonlocal games should use standard notation from the literature\\\\\\\\n- **Expansion**: use standard notation for graph expansion parameters\\\\\\\\n- **Macros** (in `macros/common.tex`): define project-specific macros and use them consistently\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe original reference controls notation whenever it gives a usable convention.\\\\\\\\nIf the blueprint needs a different symbol, index convention, or name in order to\\\\\\\\nmatch Lean, introduce it explicitly and relate it to the paper notation in the\\\\\\\\nsame paragraph.  Do not let a `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}` tag, a Lean namespace, or a file name\\\\\\\\nbe the only explanation of a changed term.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen a public Lean declaration is a formalization-only auxiliary lemma, the\\\\\\\\nblueprint should say so before listing the declaration. Each definition should introduce genuinely new mathematical content.\\\\\\\\n- **Lean namespace prefixes in prose.** Don't write \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the `LDT.PastingLemma`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" — write \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the pasting lemma\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Banned AI/Software Language (enforced in both blueprint AND Lean code)\\\\\\\\nThe blueprint reads as a **mathematical document**, not software documentation. Statement-level `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`\\\\\\\\n  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the\\\\\\\\n  proof remains tracked as incomplete.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Blueprint Structure\\\\\\\\n- `content.tex` is a router: `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.\\\\\\\\n- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`\\\\\\\\n- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Lean Blueprint Macros\\\\\\\\n- `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration\\\\\\\\n- `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Statement-level vs proof-level `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" below\\\\\\\\n- `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph\\\\\\\\n- `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)\\\\\\\\n- `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Statement-level vs proof-level `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Statement-level `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` marker.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Proof-level `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` immediately after `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok`. This file holds only\\\\\\\\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\\\\\\\\nrules never move here.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Linter warnings\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\\\\\\\\nbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\\\\\\\\nblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\\\\\\\\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\\\\\\\\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\\\\\\\\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\\\\\\\\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\\\\\\\\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\\\\\\\\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\\\\\\\\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\\\\\\\\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\\\\\\\\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\\\\\\\\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Source-faithfulness checks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\\\\\\\\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\\\\\\\\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\\\\\\\\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\\\\\\\\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\\\\\\\\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\\\\\\\\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\\\\\\\\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\\\\\\\\npositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\\\\\\\\nencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\\\\\\\\nmathematically load-bearing.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReviewers should also inspect `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{}` and `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\\\\\\\\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\\\\\\\\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\\\\\\\\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\\\\\\\\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Companion document\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\\\\\\\\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\\\\\\\\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\\\\\\\\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\\\\\\\\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\\\\\\\\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\\\\\\\\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\\\\\\\\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\\\\\\\\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\\\\\\\\n`AGENTS.md`):\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\\\\\\\\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\\\\\\\\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\\\\\\\\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\\\\\\\\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\\\\\\\\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\\\\\\\\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\\\\\\\\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\\\\\\\\n> conditional helper\\\\\\\\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\\\\\\\\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\\\\\\\\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Axiom policy\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\\\\\\\\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\\\\\\\\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\\\\\\\\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\\\\\\\\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\\\\\\\\nthe axiomatic base.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\\\\\\\\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\\\\\\\\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\\\\\\\\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\\\\\\\\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\\\\\\\\nfaithful to the paper.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\\\\\\\\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\\\\\\\\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSigns to watch for:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\\\\\\\\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\\\\\\\\n  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\\\\\\\\n- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\\\\\\\\n  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\\\\\\\\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\\\\\\\\n  semantics (e.g., a \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"projective measurement\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" definition that does not enforce\\\\\\\\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\\\\\\\\n- Intermediate lemmas These lighter\\\\\\\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\\\\\\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\\\\\\\npaper hypotheses.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Code Conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Imports\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\\\\\\\n- One import per line\\\\\\\\n- Follow existing local import style\\\\\\\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\\\\\\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\\\\\\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\\\\\\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### File structure\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. imports\\\\\\\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\\\\\\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\\\\\\\n4. declarations\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Formatting\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\\\\\\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\\\\\\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\\\\\\\n  own line\\\\\\\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\\\\\\\n  theorem statement\\\\\\\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\\\\\\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\\\\\\\\n  tactic blocks.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Naming conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\\\\\\\\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\\\\\\\\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\\\\\\\\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nProject-preferred variable names:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\\\\\\\\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\\\\\\\\n- `σ` — strategies\\\\\\\\n- `P` — projective measurements\\\\\\\\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Types and signatures\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\\\\\\\\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\\\\\\\\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\\\\\\\\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\\\\\\\\n  wrappers\\\\\\\\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Documentation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRequired:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\\\\\\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\\\\\\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\\\\\\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\lean{...}`\\\\\\\\nand `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Proof Engineering\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Search before proving\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\\\\\\\\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\\\\\\\\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\\\\\\\\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\\\\\\\\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Mathlib integration\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\\\\\\\\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\\\\\\\\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\\\\\\\\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\\\\\\\\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\\\\\\\\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\\\\\\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\\\\\\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\\\\\\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Validation ladder\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\\\\\\\n2. `lake build`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Lean-specific advice\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\\\\\\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\\\\\\\n  already in the repo\\\\\\\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\\\\\\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\\\\\\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\\\\\\\\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\\\\\\\\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\\\\\\\\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\\\\\\\\nmathematical phrase is available.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\\\\\\\\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\\\\\\\\npaper, and the local formalization. If the cited assertion is\\\\\\\\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\\\\\\\\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Proof Integrity\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\\\\\\\\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\\\\\\\\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\\\\\\\\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\\\\\\\\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\\\\\\\\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\\\\\\\\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. /-! # Collision expansion and Schwartz-Zippel bounds

This module contains the `generalizeB` theorem wrappers, finite reparametrization
and distribution bookkeeping, and the Schwartz-Zippel collision expansion that
bounds the line-collision residual.
-/

private lemma generalizeB_of_pointwise
    (params : Parameters)
    [FieldModel params.q]
    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι)
    (ψbi : QuantumState (ι × ι))
    (hpoint :
      ∀ g : Polynomial params,
        generalizeBDeviationAtPolynomial params strategy ψbi G g ≤ generalizeBError params) :
    GeneralizeBStatement params strategy ψbi G := by
  refine
    { aggregateFamilyComparison := by
        exact sddRel_unit_family_of_pointwise ψbi
          (axisParallelLineQuestionDistribution params)
          (generalizeBLeftFamily params strategy G)
          (generalizeBRightFamily params strategy G)
          (fun qu g =>
            weightedGeneralizeBLeftOperatorAtPolynomial params strategy G g qu)
          (fun qu g =>
            weightedGeneralizeBRightOperatorAtPolynomial params strategy G g qu)
          (by
            intro qu
            simp [generalizeBLeftFamily])
          (by
            intro qu
            simp [generalizeBRightFamily])
          (generalizeBError params) (by
            intro g
            simpa [generalizeBDeviationAtPolynomial] using hpoint g)
      pointwiseNormBound := hpoint
      averagedNormBound :=
        avgOver_polynomialDistribution_le_of_pointwise params
          (fun g => generalizeBDeviationAtPolynomial params strategy ψbi G g)
          (generalizeBError params) hpoint }

/-! # Polynomial-sum (cardinality-free) bounds for Section 8 transport

Cardinality-free sum-over-`g` bounds for the building blocks of the local-variance
transport chain.  These avoid the per-polynomial blow-up that one would get by
summing the pointwise estimates: instead they use both the line-measurement POVM
identity `∑_f B^ℓ_f = B^ℓ.total` and the polynomial submeasurement normalization
`∑_g G_g = G.total ≤ 1` to keep the right-register weight under control.

## Paper anchor

`references/ldt-paper/expansion.tex`, lines 282-289 (proof of `lem:generalize-b`)
and lines 317-321 (`eq:equivalent-local-variance`).
-/

/-- Polynomial-sum analogue of
`generalizeBLineCollisionTensorMass_sum_le_one`.

private lemma ev_uniformAverage_sq_le_avg
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
    (D : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    ev ψ
      ((averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α) D)ᴴ *
        averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α) D)
      ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution α) (fun a => ev ψ ((D a)ᴴ * D a)) := by
  let c : Error := 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error)
  let S : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α) D
  let x : α → Error := fun a => ev ψ ((D a)ᴴ * D a)
  have hc_nonneg : 0 ≤ c := by
    positivity
  have hx_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ x a := by
    intro a
    exact ev_adjoint_self_nonneg ψ (D a)
  have hcard : (Fintype.card α : Error) ≠ 0 := by
    positivity
  have hsumc : ∑ a : α, c = 1 := by
    unfold c
    calc
      ∑ a : α, (1 / (Fintype.card α : Error))
          = (Fintype.card α : Error) * (1 / (Fintype.card α : Error)) := by
              simp [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
      _ = 1 := by
            field_simp [hcard]
  have h_expand :
      ev ψ (Sᴴ * S)
        = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α, c * (c * ev ψ ((D a)ᴴ * D b)) := by
    have hSsum : S = ∑ a : α, c • D a := by
      ext i j
      simp [S, c, averageOperatorOverDistribution, uniformDistribution]
    have hconj :
        (∑ a : α, c • D a)ᴴ = ∑ a : α, c • (D a)ᴴ := by
      simpa using
        (Matrix.conjTranspose_sum (s := Finset.univ)
          (M := fun a : α => c • D a))
    calc
      ev ψ (Sᴴ * S)
        = ev ψ (((∑ a : α, c • D a)ᴴ) * ∑ b : α, c • D b) := by
            rw [hSsum]

# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=5000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it to 1000 on
# 2026-09-05, then to 5000 on 2026-09-30).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# only after a recorded main decision, never self-granted by a worker session. Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# workflow budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \
  scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  scripts/tests/test_lake_root.py scripts/tests/test_pre_push_hook.py \
  scripts/tests/test_ready_packets.py scripts/tests/test_merge_loss_guard.py \
  | awk '{added=$1; deleted=$2; if (added != "-") total+=added+deleted} END {print total+0}')"
if [ "${INFRA_CHANGED:-0}" -gt 5000 ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE:-}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: staged workflow-layer change is ${INFRA_CHANGED} lines (budget: 5000)."
  echo "Scope control (local/personas/main.md): the budget is PER EPISODE, not per"
  echo "commit — serial oversized commits are the same violation and show in the"
  echo "telemetry. Shrink the change, or stop for a recorded main decision that"
  echo "authorizes MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE=1; workers must not self-grant it."
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

STAGED_FILES="$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)"
if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then

fi

# Paper mirrors under references/ are byte-faithful captures of external
